blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — palonosetron CINV prevention
stem: An adult client is prescribed IV palonosetron before moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy. Which outcome is consistent with the medication's labeled use in this setting?

options.A: Prevention of both acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting when the dose is given prophylactically before the chemotherapy course begins.
options.B: Treatment of nausea and vomiting after symptoms have already developed, with no prophylactic role before moderately emetogenic chemotherapy is administered.
options.C: Prevention of the acute phase alone because delayed nausea and vomiting are outside the labeled adult indication for moderately emetogenic chemotherapy.
options.D: Reduction of chemotherapy-related pain and mucosal inflammation rather than prevention of nausea and vomiting associated with the treatment course.

rationale: Current palonosetron labeling indicates IV palonosetron in adults for prevention of both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of moderately emetogenic chemotherapy. The adult CINV dose is administered as a single IV dose beginning about 30 minutes before chemotherapy. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize IV palonosetron as prophylaxis for both acute and delayed CINV in adults receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy.
source_locator: Indications and Usage: adults—prevention of acute and delayed nausea/vomiting with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy. Dosage: 0.25 mg single IV dose beginning approximately 30 minutes before chemotherapy.
source_claim_supported: Palonosetron prevents both acute and delayed CINV in adults receiving moderately emetogenic chemotherapy and is administered prophylactically before chemotherapy.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: understand expected medication outcomes and administration timing.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed only-based cueing and rewrote all choices as complete therapeutic-outcome statements.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current palonosetron labeling; no residual absolute-word cue remains.
